_README: Overload resolution table for `torch.<op>(...)`.
Each key is a name `torch/__init__.py` hoists off `_C._VariableFunctions`.
Each value is the ordered list of aten schemas that torch's *Python*
binding exposes under that name -- not every aten overload of that name.
The distinction is load-bearing: `aten::pow` has fifteen overloads, of
which eleven (`pow.int`, `pow.float_complex`, `pow.Scalar_Scalar`, ...)
are TorchScript numeric builtins that `torch.pow` will not accept, and
listing them would make `torch.pow(2, 3)` return a float where real torch
raises TypeError.
ORDER IS THE ALGORITHM. The resolver takes the first schema that binds,
exactly as `PythonArgParser::raw_parse` does, so the order here is not
cosmetic. Two places where a plausible order is the wrong one, both
measured against torch 2.13.0 with a `TorchDispatchMode` logger rather
than reasoned about (docs/OVERLOAD.md §3):
* `.out` variants come first. They take `out` as a required kwarg-only
argument, so they bind only when the caller passed `out=`, and putting
them last would let the non-out schema swallow the call and drop the
output tensor on the floor.
* `arange.start` comes before `arange.start_step`, even though
`start_step`'s `step=1` default makes it bind a two-argument call too.
Real torch sends `torch.arange(0, 5)` to `arange.start`, and reversing
these two would name the wrong key in the work queue.
Provenance: the schema strings are `str(torch.ops.aten.<op>.<ov>._schema)`
from torch 2.13.0, transcribed here. Unlike `surface.json` this could not
come from the vendored tree -- see docs/OVERLOAD.md §2 for what the tree
does and does not carry -- so `pytests/verify_schemas.py` re-derives them
from upstream and diffs, which keeps the table from drifting silently.
That script needs real torch; the build does not.
Notes on the entries docs/NN_SURFACE.md added, where the reason is not
self-evident:
* `where` -- `.self_out` first, per the `.out` rule above. The scalar
mixes cannot shadow each other (`ScalarSelf` needs a scalar in the
second slot, `ScalarOther` in the third), so their relative order is
cosmetic, but it follows the vendored `.pyi` declaration order anyway.
The bare `where(Tensor condition) -> Tensor[]` goes last: it is the
`nonzero`-shaped overload and binds one argument, which nothing else
does.
* `bmm` carries `.dtype`/`.dtype_out` because the vendored
`_VariableFunctions.pyi` really does expose an `out_dtype` parameter.
Leaving them out would make `torch.bmm(a, b, out_dtype=...)` report
'no matching overload' where upstream accepts it.
* `rsub` is here rather than in `methods.json` because that is the route
the vendored tree takes: `torch/_tensor.py:1108` spells `Tensor.
__rsub__` as `_C._VariableFunctions.rsub(self, other)`. `1 - x` is
measured 8 times in a Llama `generate` (docs/NN_SURFACE.md §3).
Three names a model path calls are deliberately NOT here, because they
are `CompositeImplicitAutograd` upstream and an overload entry would
invent a kernel requirement upstream does not have: `linear`, `dropout`,
and `layer_norm`. All three are Python-level compositions in
`bootstrap.py` (`_install_nn`, `_install_composites`), and all three
still end at `_C._aten_dispatch`.
`layer_norm` specifically: `torch.ops.aten.layer_norm.default` exists as
a schema, but a `TorchDispatchMode` logger on torch 2.13.0 never sees it
fire -- `F.layer_norm`, `torch.layer_norm` and `nn.LayerNorm` all bottom
out at `aten.native_layer_norm.default` only, because `layer_norm` is a
thin C++ wrapper that calls `native_layer_norm` and keeps the first of
its three results. Listing `aten::layer_norm(...)` here would resolve
correctly and then name a kernel this shim will never implement, where
the honest key is one it already has -- same shape of problem as
`methods.json`'s `softmax` note. `native_layer_norm` itself has no such
mismatch (it *is* the leaf op), so it gets a normal entry above.
`split` above lists only `split.Tensor` (the int-size overload), not the
full `torch.ops.aten.split.*` overload set. That is deliberate and
different from `methods.json`'s `split`, which lists both `split.Tensor`
and `split_with_sizes`: `_VariableFunctions.split` (`torch._VF.split`)
is, measured, only ever called by the vendored tree with an int --
`torch/_tensor.py:Tensor.split` is what looks at the argument type and
routes a list/tuple to `torch._VF.split_with_sizes` instead, which is
why that op gets its own `split_with_sizes` key rather than being folded
in here.
docs/SPELLINGS.md §6 notes on `any`/`div`/`mean`/`sum`, measured with a
`TorchDispatchMode` logger on torch 2.13.0 rather than reasoned about:
* `any` -- the `.out` group's internal order is not the same as the
non-`.out` group's. `any(x, out=o)` (no `dim`) resolves to
`any.all_out`, not `any.dims_out`, even though `dims_out`'s `dim`
parameter is also optional and would otherwise shadow it -- `all_out`
simply comes first in the declaration order the real arg parser
tries. `any.dims_out`/`any.out` follow, keyed off `dim` being a
list/tuple versus a plain `int`, mirroring the non-`.out` group below.
* `sum` -- `aten::sum.out` (the no-`dim` `.out` overload) is listed in
`torch.ops.aten.sum.overloads()` but **`torch.sum` never reaches
it**: `torch.sum(x, out=o)` raises `TypeError` from the real arg
parser before any dispatch happens, because the no-`dim` Python
overload plainly does not accept `out=`. `sum.out` is left out of
this table for that reason -- listing it would name a path upstream
itself does not expose, the same complaint `layer_norm` above makes
about a schema that resolves to a kernel this shim will never reach.
`mean` does not have this gap -- `mean(x, out=o)` (no `dim`) resolves
to `mean.dtype_out`, a real reachable overload -- so `mean` lists all
four.
`transpose`, `permute` and `sub` came from docs/DECOMP.md §4: they are
not names a model path calls, they are names *upstream's own
decomposition rules* call while the decomposition pass runs them. The
rule for `aten.t.default` calls `torch.transpose`, the rule for
`aten.transpose.int` calls `torch.permute`, and the rule for
`aten.rsub.Scalar` calls `torch.sub`. Every one of the three names an
aten key this shim already implements, so the entry is the whole fix --
no kernel is invented. `sub` mirrors `add` above and omits
`sub.Scalar_out` for the same reason `add` omits `add.Scalar_out`.
`log` (docs/ARCH20.md §4) is the second op after `pow` where the
`aten::` packet is mostly TorchScript numerics, and it is a sharper
case: **fourteen of `aten::log`'s sixteen overloads are scalar
builtins** (`log.int`, `log.float`, `log.Scalar`, `log.int_float`,
`log.complex_complex`, ...), and `torch.log` accepts none of them --
`torch.log(2.0)` is a TypeError from the arg parser upstream. Only the
two `Tensor` schemas are listed, and the `.out` one comes first per the
rule above. Listing the numerics would turn a call upstream refuses into
a call this shim answers, which is the divergence direction that costs
the most to find. `exp`, added in the same round for `mamba`, has the
same shape (four of its overloads are numerics) and gets the same
treatment; both kernels already existed, so both entries are the whole
fix.
`stack` (cohere, docs/ARCH20.md §5) had a kernel and no spelling --
`aten.stack.default` has been in `IMPLEMENTED` and golden-compared since
docs/ARCH.md, and `torch.stack(...)` still refused. That is the pattern
the coverage sweep is structurally unable to see: it traces on upstream
and asks whether every *dispatched* operator is implemented here, so a
missing `torch.<name>` never appears in it.
`constant_pad_nd` (bert, §2) is the reverse -- a genuinely new kernel.
Its `.out` sibling is omitted for the reason `sum.out` is: this shim has
no out-variant kernel, and `F.pad` never asks for one.
